finalText:
Diagnosis: `c070-client` has broken per-pod DNS settings. The Service and server backend are healthy; name resolution from the client is failing because the pod overrides cluster DNS with an invalid resolver and search domain.

- Root cause
  - `pod/c070-client` sets `dnsPolicy: None` with custom `dnsConfig`, overriding cluster DNS.
  - It uses `nameservers: [203.0.113.1]` and `searches: [bad.local]`, which prevents normal in-cluster resolution of `c070-server-svc` / `c070-server-svc.siclaw-eval-yye-20260602.svc`.

- Concrete evidence
  - Client pod DNS config:
    - `dnsPolicy: None`
    - `dnsConfig.nameservers: 203.0.113.1`
    - `dnsConfig.searches: bad.local`
  - Service wiring is correct:
    - `service/c070-server-svc` selector: `app: c070-server`
    - port `80 -> targetPort 8080`
    - Endpoint exists: `172.16.36.208:8080`
  - Server pod exists and is healthy:
    - `pod/c070-server` is `Running`, same node, IP `172.16.36.208`
  - No `c070` NetworkPolicy exists in the namespace, so there is no evidence of policy-based DNS/service blocking for this case.

- Impact / scope
  - Directly affects `pod/c070-client`.
  - Any lookup or connection by service name from that pod will fail or be misdirected; the Service itself and server pod are not broken.

- Confidence
  - High.

- Safe remediation suggestion
  - Remove the custom DNS override from `c070-client` and use normal cluster DNS (`dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst`), or set `dnsConfig` to the cluster DNS service and valid cluster search domains.
  - After correction, verify that `c070-client` resolves `c070-server-svc` and reaches `c070-server-svc:80`.

Diagnosis: `c070-client` has broken per-pod DNS settings. The Service and server backend are healthy; name resolution from the client is failing because the pod overrides cluster DNS with an invalid resolver and search domain.

- Root cause
  - `pod/c070-client` sets `dnsPolicy: None` with custom `dnsConfig`, overriding cluster DNS.
  - It uses `nameservers: [203.0.113.1]` and `searches: [bad.local]`, which prevents normal in-cluster resolution of `c070-server-svc` / `c070-server-svc.siclaw-eval-yye-20260602.svc`.

- Concrete evidence
  - Client pod DNS config:
    - `dnsPolicy: None`
    - `dnsConfig.nameservers: 203.0.113.1`
    - `dnsConfig.searches: bad.local`
  - Service wiring is correct:
    - `service/c070-server-svc` selector: `app: c070-server`
    - port `80 -> targetPort 8080`
    - Endpoint exists: `172.16.36.208:8080`
  - Server pod exists and is healthy:
    - `pod/c070-server` is `Running`, same node, IP `172.16.36.208`
  - No `c070` NetworkPolicy exists in the namespace, so there is no evidence of policy-based DNS/service blocking for this case.

- Impact / scope
  - Directly affects `pod/c070-client`.
  - Any lookup or connection by service name from that pod will fail or be misdirected; the Service itself and server pod are not broken.

- Confidence
  - High.

- Safe remediation suggestion
  - Remove the custom DNS override from `c070-client` and use normal cluster DNS (`dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst`), or set `dnsConfig` to the cluster DNS service and valid cluster search domains.
  - After correction, verify that `c070-client` resolves `c070-server-svc` and reaches `c070-server-svc:80`.
